minutes.headline: Committee agreed to send the select board its cost questions and intent to develop a school environmental policy.
minutes.summary: The committee heard public comment on SEL, school safety and a Thanksgiving food drive, then a quarterly ESSER 2 and 3 grant update with no action requested. It discussed the town's environmental policy and the municipal building concepts, including Turkey Hill, early childhood programs and gym space. It authorized a communication to the select board, planned a statement to the building committee, and went into executive session.

public_comment.topic: Criticised SEL curriculum and the pending equity audit, responding to a committee member's earlier remarks; called it a program of equity and cited failed leadership.
Supports parental opt-out of SEL; advocates expanding the school resource officer and comfort dog program to the other two buildings and finding funding.
Thanksgiving food drive with the food pantry, with each building collecting specific items.
public_comment.stated_role: president of the Lunenburg Educators Association

public_comment.topic: Urged parents to report bullying to principals and teachers rather than on Facebook.

votes.motion: Approve the August 24th regular meeting minutes.
Accept the ESSER budget report as presented.
Authorize the chair and superintendent to communicate to the select board the committee's questions and intent to develop a complementary environmental policy.
Go into executive session to discuss deployment of security personnel or devices, and adjourn after.

budget_items.what_was_said: The grant funds math specialist, targeted math teacher, guidance counselor, social worker and part-time IT technician, and expires September 30, 2023.
A surplus is projected, partly from shifting IT technician salary to the FY22 budget, with a possible further amount if the after-school program is implemented.
Expires September 30, 2024; funds positions and tutors; a larger surplus is projected from turnover, hiring difficulty and unspent fringe.
Possible Chromebooks, consumables, mentoring stipend, extending positions in FY24, split AC units at Turkey Hill and technology upgrades; none advocated for action tonight.
Middle school social worker and math specialist are already budgeted in FY24 ESSER funds; high school targeted math teacher and primary guidance counselor have no funding after this year.
Finance committee reported free cash certified, described as another bumper crop.
figures_as_heard: two million eight hundred and thirty eight thousand five hundred dollars

budget_items.what_was_said: A member referenced excludable debt over ten years and capital plan money projected for Turkey Hill, saying it may cost more.
A member asked what cost would be associated with adopting the environmental policy; costs to be raised with the select board.

decisions.decision: Bus policy change deferred until the bus contractor reports maximum capacity.
Chair and superintendent will send the select board the facilities director's statement plus a note on cost and intent to develop a complementary policy.
Chair will draft a statement to the municipal building committee, with feedback to it before Monday and a formal statement after the next meeting.
Next meeting will be fully remote and start at 6:45; municipal building and environmental policy return to the agenda.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to have the chair and superintendent send the select board its cost questions and its intent to develop a complementary environmental policy.
The committee voted to accept the ESSER budget report as presented, after a quarterly update on the ESSER 2 and 3 grants in which no action was requested.
Members discussed the municipal building concepts and Turkey Hill, and the chair will draft a statement to the municipal building committee.
A bus policy change was deferred until the bus contractor reports its maximum capacity.
The next meeting will be fully remote, starting at 6:45, with the municipal building and environmental policy returning to the agenda.

why_it_matters: ESSER grants fund several school positions and expire in 2023 and 2024, so a resident may be asked later to vote on whether the town budget picks up those positions.
The municipal building and Turkey Hill plans are tied to excludable debt and capital plan money, which could reach a tax bill if they come to a vote.
watch_next: The next School Committee meeting, fully remote at 6:45, where the municipal building and environmental policy return to the agenda.
The chair's formal statement to the municipal building committee, due after the next meeting, with feedback to it before Monday.
